To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) mastery goal structure and orientation were positively related to all adaptive outcomes and negatively related to all non adaptive outcomes, (2) performance approach goal structure was positively related to procrastination, and (3) performance approach and avoidance goal orientations were positively related to procrastinating, and negatively related to persistence and choice.

mastery goal structures and mastery goal orientations are associated with positive outcomes, while performance goal structures and performance goal orientations are associated more weakly with positive outcomes.

(a) students' perceived mastery goal structures and mastery goal orientations were related to adaptive motivational and cognitive outcomes in mathematics; (b) students' perceived performance goal structures and performance goal orientations were related in different ways to different motivational and cognitive outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a more complete achievement goal theory, one that includes the goal structures and goal orientations of students and teachers.
the question of how different components of the achievement goal framework (e.g., goal structures, goal orientations, outcomes) relate to one another.
the development of a model that integrates the two most important theories of achievement motivation, namely goal structures and goal orientations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mastery goal structure and mastery goal orientation are related to adaptive outcomes across all domains.

mastery goal structures and mastery goal orientations are associated with adaptive motivational and cognitive outcomes, while performance goal structures and performance goal orientations are associated, in some cases, with adaptive and in other cases with non adaptive motivational and cognitive outcome variables.

mastery structures and orientations are related to a wide array of adaptive motivational, cognitive, and achievement outcomes, while performance structures and orientations are not consistently associated with adaptive outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mastery goal structures and orientations are important for students to achieve in school.

mastery structure and orientation are important for promoting students' motivation and cognitive engagement, and that performance goal structure and orientation are not necessarily adaptive for students' learning and achievement in mathematics, and may in fact be harmful in some cases.

students who perceive a mastery goal structure in their classroom and have a strong mastery goal orientation are more likely to be motivated to learn and persist at learning mathematics, to be engaged in the learning process, and to perform well in mathematics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the goal structure of a classroom is a key predictor of students' motivation and cognitive engagement.
achievement goal theory is an important and valuable framework for understanding students' motivation and learning.
the theory can be advanced by using goal structures and goal orientations together.
